proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 F_c(h,z)=(1+c)\sum_{j=1}^Jp_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Rh_j,Rz_j),
 \qquad 0<c<\infty,
\]
and let \(F_\infty(h,z)=G(h,z)(1)\). By the hard-endpoint lemma and the definition of the compactified path, on \(D_{\mathbf a}(h)\),
\[
 G(h,z)(0)=L_{\mathbf a}(h),\qquad
 \lim_{c\downarrow0}F_c(h,z)=L_{\mathbf a}(h),\qquad
 S(h,z)=\max\{L_{\mathbf a}(h),U_h(z)\}.                 \tag{1}
\]
The benchmark-support and stratum-mass assumptions give \(b_{ja}>0\) and \(p_j>0\) for every \(j,a\).

We first locate all possible atoms. Fix \(v\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(s>0\). Differentiating the finite sum in the definition of \(F_c\), using \(Dq_{c,b}(w)=c^{-1}C\{q_{c,b}(w)\}\), gives
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}F_c(h,sv)
 =\frac{s(1+c)}{c}\sum_{j=1}^Jp_j
 (Rv_j)^{\top}C\{q_{c,b_j}(R(h_j+sv_j))\}Rv_j.          \tag{2}
\]
Every coordinate of the Gibbs vector is positive. For a positive probability vector \(r\), \(x^{\top}C(r)x\) is the variance of the coordinates of \(x\) under \(r\), and hence vanishes exactly when those coordinates are constant. Since some \(v_j\ne0\), the vector \(Rv_j=(0,v_j^{\top})^{\top}\) is not constant. Thus (2) is strictly positive. At the quadratic endpoint, the matrix inequality in the high-endpoint lemma similarly yields
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}F_\infty(h,sv)
 =s\sum_{j=1}^Jp_jv_j^{\top}R^{\top}C(b_j)Rv_j
 \ge s\beta^2\sum_{j=1}^Jp_j\|v_j\|_2^2>0.             \tag{3}
\]

The intersection of \(D_{\mathbf a}(h)\) with a ray \(\{sv:s>0\}\) is an interval because it is the intersection of finitely many strict affine inequalities in \(s\). Suppose \(s_1<s_2\) belong to that interval and \(U_h(s_1v)>L_{\mathbf a}(h)\). Compactified path continuity and (1) imply that the supremum defining \(U_h(s_1v)\) is attained at some \(t_*\in(0,1]\). Equations (2)--(3), at the corresponding finite or infinite temperature, then give
\[
 U_h(s_2v)\ge G(h,s_2v)(t_*)>G(h,s_1v)(t_*)=U_h(s_1v). \tag{4}
\]
Also \(U_h(sv)\ge L_{\mathbf a}(h)\) by the first limit in (1). Therefore, for every \(q\ne L_{\mathbf a}(h)\), each radial section of
\[
 D_{\mathbf a}(h)\cap\{z:U_h(z)=q\}                  \tag{5}
\]
contains at most one point and has one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. Polar Fubini applied to (5) shows that (5) is Lebesgue null. The finitely many decision boundaries are affine hyperplanes. Since \(V\in\mathcal K_V\subset\mathbb S_{++}^d\), \(Z_V\) has a Lebesgue density, so those boundaries and (5) are Gaussian null.

Outside the decision boundaries, the hard cells partition \(\mathbb R^d\). On a cell with \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)>q\), (1) makes \(\{S=q\}\) empty. On a cell with \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)<q\), that event is contained in the null set (5). On a cell with \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)=q\), (1) gives the exact equivalence
\[
 \{S(h,Z_V)=q\}\cap\{Z_V\in D_{\mathbf a}(h)\}
 =\{Z_V\in D_{\mathbf a}(h),\ U_h(Z_V)\le q\}.       \tag{6}
\]
Summing (6) over the \(K^J\) cells proves both the displayed atom formula and the assertion that no other atom is possible.

We next construct the collision witness. Set
\[
 r=\frac{b_1}{b_0}=\frac1{64},\qquad
 \mathcal H_0=[1,5/4]^2,
\]
and write the augmented binary true reward as \((0,h)\). At error \(z=-2h\), the estimated reward is \((0,-h)\). With \(x=h/c\), direct substitution in the log-sum-exp formula gives
\[
 \frac{\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}}{h}
 =1+\frac1x\log\frac{r+e^{-x}}{1+re^{-x}}
   -\frac{2re^{-x}}{1+re^{-x}}.                       \tag{7}
\]
We prove, uniformly for \(1\le h\le5/4\), that
\[
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}<h,qquad c>0.       \tag{8}
\]
If \(0<x\le2\), then along the segment from \((0,h)\) to \((0,-h)\) the action-one odds are at most \(re^x\). The integral representation in the Bregman-identity lemma therefore gives
\[
 \ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}
 \le \frac{4h^2}{c}\int_0^1sre^x\,ds
 =2hxr e^x.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac{(1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}}h
 \le2re^x(x+h)\le\frac{13e^2}{128}<1,                \tag{9}
\]
where the last strict inequality follows from \(e<3\). If \(x\ge2\), put
\[
 D(x)=\log\frac{1+re^{-x}}{r+e^{-x}}.
\]
Its derivative is
\[
 D'(x)=\frac{e^{-x}(1-r^2)}{(r+e^{-x})(1+re^{-x})}>0. \tag{10}
\]
Moreover, \(e^2>7\) and \(e^{5/4}<4\) imply
\[
 D(2)>\log4>\frac54\ge h.                             \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, \(r+e^{-2}<1/64+1/7<1/4\), while the numerator in \(D(2)\) exceeds one. Rewriting (7) now yields
\[
 \ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}
 =h-cD(x)-\frac{2hre^{-x}}{1+re^{-x}}<h(1-c).
\]
Here \(c=h/x\le5/8<1\), and hence
\[
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,-2h)\}<h(1-c^2)<h.
\]
This completes the proof of (8). All numerical inequalities in (9)--(11) follow, for example, from the positive-term exponential series and the geometric remainder bound.

For \(h=(h_1,h_2)\in\mathcal H_0\), define
\[
 z^{(1)}(h)=(-2h_1,0),\qquad z^{(2)}(h)=(0,-2h_2).
\]
At \(z^{(k)}(h)\), exactly stratum \(k\) chooses the wrong hard action, so its hard level is
\[
 L_k(h)=p_kh_k=\frac{h_k}{2}.                          \tag{12}
\]
Equation (8) proves \(F_c\{h,z^{(k)}(h)\}<L_k(h)\) for every finite \(c>0\). We now verify that this inequality persists on an open neighborhood uniformly over all temperatures and all \(h\in\mathcal H_0\).

Choose a fixed neighborhood small enough that the estimated contrast in the wrong stratum is at most \(-\kappa\) and that in the correct stratum is at least \(\kappa\), for some \(\kappa>0\) independent of \(h\). For a scalar perturbation \(z\), put \(w=h+z\). The exact binary formula
\[
 \ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,z)\}
 =c\log\frac{1+re^{h/c}}{1+re^{w/c}}
   +z\frac{re^{w/c}}{1+re^{w/c}}                     \tag{13}
\]
and \(0\le\log(1+y)\le y\) give, uniformly in that neighborhood as \(c\downarrow0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,z)\}
 &=h+c(h+\log r)+c^2\log r
   +O\!\left((1+c)(c+|z|)r^{-1}e^{-\kappa/c}\right)
 &&(w\le-\kappa),\\
 (1+c)\ell_{c,b}\{(0,h),(0,z)\}
 &=O\!\left((1+c)(c+|z|)r^{-1}e^{-\kappa/c}\right)
 &&(w\ge\kappa).
 \end{aligned}                                        \tag{14}
\]
Since \(h+\log r\le5/4-\log64<0\), the negative term linear in \(c\) in the wrong stratum dominates the two exponentially small remainders in (14). Thus there are \(c_0>0\) and a uniform neighborhood of each \(z^{(k)}(h)\) on which \(F_c(h,z)<L_k(h)\) for \(0<c\le c_0\).

On every compact interval \([c_0,C_0]\), (8), continuity, and compactness of \([1,5/4]^2\times[c_0,C_0]\) give a strictly positive uniform margin at the central points; uniform continuity extends it to a common neighborhood. At the remaining endpoint, the high-temperature lemma gives uniform convergence to
\[
 F_\infty\{h,z^{(k)}(h)\}
 =\frac12p_k(2h_k)^2b_0b_1
 =b_0b_1h_k^2<\frac{h_k}{2}=L_k(h),                   \tag{15}
\]
because \(2b_0b_1h_k<1\). Its explicit \(O(c^{-1})\) remainder, followed by uniform continuity on a bounded neighborhood, supplies \(C_0<\infty\) and the same strict inequality for \(c\ge C_0\). Combining the small, compact-intermediate, and large temperature ranges yields a number \(\delta>0\), independent of \(h\), such that the open cubes
\[
 B_k(h)=\{z:\|z-z^{(k)}(h)\|_\infty<\delta\},\qquad k=1,2,                \tag{16}
\]
remain in the corresponding hard cell and satisfy
\[
 S(h,z)=L_k(h)\quad\text{for every }z\in B_k(h).       \tag{17}
\]

The centers in (16) range over a compact set. The standard bivariate Gaussian density is therefore bounded below by a positive constant on the union of the closures of smaller concentric cubes. Their Lebesgue volumes are fixed and positive, so for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_0}P\{Z_{I_2}\in B_k(h)\}\ge\eta,
 \qquad k=1,2.                                        \tag{18}
\]

Let \(\delta_m\downarrow0\), set
\[
 h_m=(1,1+\delta_m),\qquad q_m=\frac12,
 \qquad x_m=\frac{\delta_m}{2}.
\]
By (12), the first atom is at the excluded left endpoint \(q_m\), while the second is at \(q_m+x_m\). Equations (17)--(18) give
\[
 P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\le q_m+x_m\}
 \ge P\{Z_{I_2}\in B_2(h_m)\}\ge\eta.               \tag{19}
\]

For completeness, these fixed inputs arise from legal causal laws. Draw \(X\) uniformly on two strata and \(A\) uniformly and independently conditional on \(X\). Conditional on \(X=j\), take independent potential-outcome residuals with values \(\pm1/(2\sqrt2)\), and set
\[
 Y(0)=\epsilon_0,qquad Y(1)=\frac{h_j}{\sqrt n}+\epsilon_1,
 \qquad Y=Y(A).
\]
Rows are i.i.d.; consistency and conditional randomization hold by construction; \(|Y(a)|<2\); the stratum and action probabilities equal \(1/2\); the benchmark support equals \(1/65\); and the local remainder is zero. Each residual variance is \(1/8\), so the contrast-score variance in stratum \(j\) is
\[
 \frac1{p_j}\left(\frac{1/8}{e_{j1}}+\frac{1/8}{e_{j0}}\right)
 =2\left(\frac14+\frac14\right)=1.                  \tag{20}
\]
Scores from different strata have zero product, hence \(V_n=I_2\). Thus every law used by (19) belongs to the declared model class.

If a uniform atom-removed modulus \(A(x)\downarrow0\) followed from the frozen assumptions, applying it to (19) would give \(\eta\le A(x_m)\to0\), a contradiction. Finally, the certified-calibration theorem verifies a one-sided lower-CDF inequality directly and its fallback uses only a Gaussian tail bound. Neither step invokes a small-interval modulus. Its certificate therefore remains valid at the atoms characterized in (6), whereas a two-sided conversion from probability error to a prescribed critical-value width is unavailable under the frozen assumptions alone.

added_lemmas.statement: Class-transfer corollary. The positive uniform path law and certified-calibration theorem remain restricted to the declared class \(\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\) with fixed finite strata and actions, known randomized propensities, bounded outcomes, local root-sample-size contrasts, and a supplied nonsingular covariance envelope; they are not positive claims over the full model class studied by \citet{FangRidderXie2025}. In the converse direction, the fixed two-stratum binary witness in the no-uniform-modulus theorem satisfies the Fang--Ridder--Xie randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses. Hence, over that broader published class, there is no uniform function \(A:(0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) with \(A(x)\downarrow0\) that bounds every atom-removed increment \(P\{q<S(h,Z_V)\le q+x\}\). Consequently no uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion whose validity is based on such a modulus follows over the broader class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The positive scope statement follows directly from the quantifiers of the uniform path law: its supremum is over \(\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\), whose definition fixes finite \(J,K\), cell-mean sampling, the local contrast structure, and the covariance envelope. The certified-calibration theorem takes the corresponding finite-dimensional effective record as input. Neither theorem asserts an achievability result after those restrictions are removed, so this corollary does not enlarge either positive theorem.

For the converse, use the causal laws constructed in the proof of the no-uniform-modulus theorem. They have two strata and two actions; conditional treatment probabilities and stratum probabilities are both \(1/2\); potential outcomes are uniformly bounded; assignment is conditionally independent of the potential-outcome schedule; consistency holds; and both benchmark probabilities are at least \(1/65\). Thus the witness satisfies the randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses of the class studied by \citet{FangRidderXie2025}. In particular, the witness is a subclass member of that broader class, even though the positive theorems of this note remain stated only on the smaller declared finite-cell class.

Suppose a uniform atom-removed modulus existed over the broader class. Restricting its law, parameter, covariance, threshold, and interval-width quantifiers to the witness would give
\[
 P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\le q_m+x_m\}\le A(x_m)
 \quad\text{with}\quad A(x_m)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The no-uniform-modulus theorem instead gives a constant \(\eta>0\) for which the left side is at least \(\eta\) for every \(m\), a contradiction. A uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion whose proof premise is that same modulus would restrict in exactly the same way and would require the contradicted inequality. Therefore the negative conclusion transfers upward to the broader published class, while no positive path-law or calibration claim is transferred upward.
added_lemmas.justification: This corollary records the asymmetric class transfer: the positive finite-cell theory stays restricted, while a counterexample transfers to every larger class containing it.
added_lemmas.gap: The published model is broader than the declared positive theorem's class, so positive achievability cannot be lifted by inclusion; the binary witness makes the negative inclusion argument exact.
added_lemmas.consumer: Readers can distinguish the scope of the positive inference guarantee from the broader scope of the anti-concentration impossibility.

proposed.statement:
For fixed \(h\in\mathcal H\), define the open hard cells \(D_{\mathbf a}(h)=\{z:\ a_j\text{ is the unique maximizer of }R(h_j+z_j)\text{ for every }j\}\), their hard levels \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)=\sum_jp_j[\max_r(Rh_j)_r-(Rh_j)_{a_j}]\), and \(U_h(z)=\sup_{0<t\le1}G(h,z)(t)\). Then every atom of \(S(h,Z_V)\) is at one of the finitely many values \(L_{\mathbf a}(h)\), and
\[
 P\{S(h,Z_V)=q\}=\sum_{\mathbf a:L_{\mathbf a}(h)=q}P\{Z_V\in D_{\mathbf a}(h),\ U_h(Z_V)\le q\}.
\]
The frozen assumptions do not imply a uniform atom-removed modulus. In particular, there are legal fixed inputs with \(J=K=2\), \(p=(1/2,1/2)\), common benchmark \(b=(64/65,1/65)\), \(\beta=1/65\), \(\mathcal H=[1,5/4]^2\), and \(\mathcal K_V=\{I_2\}\), constants \(\eta>0\), and sequences \(h_m\in\mathcal H\), \(q_m\in\mathbb R\), and \(x_m\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\le q_m+x_m\}\ge\eta.
\]
Consequently no \(A(x)\downarrow0\) having the requested uniform property follows in general, even after the atom at \(q\) is removed. The one-sided probability certificate of \(\mathsf A\) remains valid, including at all enumerated atoms, but the frozen assumptions alone do not supply a two-sided least-favorable quantile bracket of prescribed value width.
proposed.justification: The theorem identifies every hard-cell atom, proves by a fixed legal binary design that removing the atom at the left endpoint does not restore uniform small-interval control, and supplies the witness used for upward negative class transfer.
proposed.gap: Gaussian-process anti-concentration does not apply to this nonlinear supremum, and the explicit collision witness proves that the desired modulus is false under the declared class rather than merely unproved.
proposed.consumer: Implementers retain the atom-safe one-sided certificate; readers also see why a two-sided critical-value tolerance needs additional separation even in broader classes containing the witness.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses positivity of cell masses and benchmarks, the Bregman identity, compactified continuity, the high-temperature endpoint, and the primitive causal assumptions used to certify the witness; these dependencies must be explicit.

proposed.comparator_claim: For fixed positive \(\lambda\), \(nR_\lambda(\widehat\theta)\) converges to one-half of a Gaussian quadratic form; the surrounding randomized model includes the binary witness used here.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Fang--Ridder--Xie row must distinguish the unextended positive theorem from the proved upward-transfer negative result; all other comparator positions are preserved.

prose_updates.tldr: On a declared fixed finite-cell randomized causal subclass, benchmark-centered Gibbs rules form one compact continuous regret path with hard-lottery and projected-quadratic endpoints. The note proves a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation and a terminating, machine-checkable one-sided calibration that remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. The positive path law and calibration are not extended to the full Fang--Ridder--Xie model class. In the converse direction, an exact cellwise atom formula and a legal two-stratum binary collision witness rule out a uniform atom-removed small-interval modulus; because that witness satisfies the published class's randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, this negative conclusion transfers upward to the broader class.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while hard assignment and predetermined softmax sequences are studied separately. No published result supplies a quantitative joint path law or a certified atom-safe critical value over the full penalty menu. Standard Gaussian-supremum anti-concentration also cannot handle the colliding hard-cell atoms exhibited here, including within the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.
project_justification.niche: For fixed finite strata and actions, the lottery problem becomes a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic with nonlinear Gaussian interior coordinates, benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and a quadratic opposite endpoint. The same finite subclass is rich enough to expose positive-mass hard-cell atoms whose levels collide, so it supports both computable positive inference and an upward-transfer impossibility result.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the finite-cell Gaussian path approximation, both endpoint limits, the selection bridge, and a terminating lower-CDF certificate with an analytic fallback. It also proves the exact atom formula and a fixed legal counterexample to uniform atom-removed anti-concentration. Positive achievability remains confined to the declared finite-cell class; only the negative conclusion transfers to the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class that contains the witness.

prose_updates.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty in a broader randomized assignment model and leaves data-driven penalty choice open. The present positive path law and certified calibration require the narrower declared fixed finite-cell subclass and are not extensions over the full published class. The relation is asymmetric: the two-stratum binary counterexample satisfies Fang--Ridder--Xie's randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, so the failure of uniform atom-removed anti-concentration transfers upward. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis studies one predetermined diverging smoother for a different scalar target. Hirano--Porter supplies a binary shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato and Giessing treat Gaussian-process suprema, whereas the present supremum is nonlinear and has colliding hard-cell atoms. Fang--Santos studies directional irregularity; Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki supply Gaussian integration components; and Kang supplies simultaneous-band selection logic. None yields the atom-safe continuum certificate proved on the declared subclass here.
prose_updates.interpretation: The positive result is deliberately one-sided and deliberately subclass-specific: within fixed finite randomized cells, one auditable critical value covers the entire normalized oracle-regret path and therefore every measurable temperature choice. The negative result has broader reach. Nearby local states retain positive atoms at hard-cell levels that approach one another, so no vanishing atom-removed modulus, and hence no conversion based on one, can hold uniformly over any larger model class containing this witness, including the Fang--Ridder--Xie class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The work-capped algorithm always terminates because it can issue an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback, and its one-sided lower-CDF certificate remains valid at atoms. It need not approximate the ideal least-favorable critical value within a prescribed numerical width. Colliding positive-mass atoms prove that the missing uniform atom-removed modulus cannot be recovered from the declared assumptions or from the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie hypotheses containing the witness. A two-sided value-width guarantee therefore needs an additional separation, restricted-state, or explicit atom-structure condition; the positive path law itself remains confined to the finite-cell subclass.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Positive uniform approximation and calibration are claimed only for fixed finite strata and actions, known randomized propensities, positive benchmark probabilities, positive cell masses, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, root-sample-size localization, and a supplied covariance spectrum bounded away from zero. They are not claimed for the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class, boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing dimension, disappearing cells, or continuous covariates without prespecified finite stratification. The commitment-savings display is conditional on such cells. The upward class transfer applies only to the negative result: the binary witness lies in the broader published class, so that class cannot support the rejected uniform modulus or a probability-to-critical-value conversion based on it.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem identifies all hard-cell atoms, proves a fixed legal collision witness, and supplies the counterexample used for upward negative class transfer.
statement_notes.gap: Standard Gaussian anti-concentration does not cover this nonlinear supremum, and the collision proves that a vanishing atom-removed modulus is false rather than merely unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: Implementers retain atom-safe one-sided calibration while recognizing that prescribed two-sided value accuracy needs additional structure.

statement_notes.justification: This corollary records the asymmetric class transfer: positive finite-cell achievability stays restricted, whereas the binary impossibility witness transfers to every larger class containing it.
statement_notes.gap: A result on a subclass does not lift positive achievability to a broader published class, but a counterexample inside the subclass does lift a uniform impossibility.
statement_notes.consumer: Readers can separate the narrow scope of the positive inference guarantee from the broader scope of the anti-concentration obstruction.
